fields that exceed a configured size threshold, storing these values directly in the Kafka message can increase broker memory pressure, network I/O, and storage costs. The Debezium S3 large message post processor (
) offloads large field values to Amazon S3 and replaces the in-message value with a compact inline reference. Downstream consumers can use the inline reference to fetch the original value from S3.

The post processor generates a unique S3 object key for each offloaded field by incorporating the values from the change event’s source information block. Because the source information block is connector-specific, the post processor dynamically iterates all fields defined in the source schema and incorporates their names and values into the object key.

Connector implementations must ensure that the source information block contains a set of fields whose values uniquely identify each change event. If two events from the same source produce identical source block values, their object keys collide, causing one event’s offloaded value to overwrite the other, leading to data loss. The core Debezium connectors satisfy this requirement, but non-core connectors might not. If the source information block is
or contains no fields, a unique object key cannot be resolved and the field value is passed through as-is.
By default, the post processor offloads all
fields that meet the size threshold. You can restrict which fields are eligible for offloading by using the

These properties accept comma-separated lists of regular expressions that match field names. If an include list is specified, only fields whose names match are eligible for offloading. If an exclude list is specified, fields whose names match are excluded. Do not set both properties at the same time; if both are set, the include list takes precedence.
